test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Raj’s monthly income is ₹50,000. He spends 40% of his income on household expenses and saves the remaining amount. If his income increases by 10%, and his expenditure on household expenses remains the same percentage of his income, calculate the amount (in ₹) he saves after the increment.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income increases by 10% ⇒ new income = 50000 × 1.10 = 55000

Expenditure = 40% ⇒ savings = 60%

New savings = 60% of 55000

= 0.6 × 55000 = 33000

**∴ Answer = 33000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original income = 50000, Expenditure = 40%

Income increases by 10%

**Formula used:**

Savings = Income × (1 − Expenditure%)

**Calculation:**

⇒ New income = 50000 × (1 + 10/100)

⇒ New income = 50000 × 1.10 = 55000

⇒ Savings% = 100 − 40 = 60%

⇒ Savings = 55000 × 60/100

⇒ Savings = 33000

**∴ The correct answer is 33000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Savings Formula

Savings = Income − Expenditure or Income × (1 − expense%).

Percentage Increase

New value = Original × (1 + increase/100).

Complement Rule

If expenditure is 40%, savings automatically become 60%.
